source_text:
Synthetic note v1
For two equally likely outcomes 0 and 2, the mean is 1. Variance averages squared deviations from the mean, so variance is 1.
Probabilities must be nonnegative and sum to one; finite support gives finite second moments.
Shifting both outcomes by a constant changes the mean but leaves variance unchanged. Multiplication by a scales variance by a squared.
This finite example establishes no universal statement about unbiasedness of arbitrary estimators.
summary: The two equally likely outcomes are 0 and 2. Their mean is 1. Variance is 0 because signed deviations cancel. This proves all noisy estimators are unbiased. I focus on the shift.
